learning_need: Experiential introduction to rhythm, melody, harmony, basslines and song structure through direct browser creation
decision_rationale: Learning Music earns a core slot because its pedagogy is direct and productive: learners make beats, melodies and harmonies in the browser rather than only reading about them. It complements formal theory and synthesis rather than duplicating either.
marginal_value: Adds beginner-friendly music creation and composition practice with almost no setup friction.
provider_concentration_notes: Ableton has two admitted routes, but they cover separate competencies: musical construction versus synthesis/sound design.
coverage_notes: Pairs naturally with musictheory.net for formal theory and Learning Synths for sound design.

decision_rationale: Learning Synths serves a distinct sound-design role through direct manipulation of a browser synthesizer. Oscillators, filters, envelopes and modulation become immediately audible and interactive, producing much stronger practice than a passive synthesis overview.
marginal_value: Adds hands-on synthesis and timbre design not covered by the broader music-creation course.
provider_concentration_notes: Second Ableton slot is justified by a materially separate learning outcome.
coverage_notes: A specialist complement to Learning Music and formal theory.

learning_need: Structured music theory, notation, harmony, ear training and configurable drills
decision_rationale: musictheory.net is the strongest pure theory/practice system in the pool. Its sequence extends from notation and rhythm through scales, intervals, chords and analysis, while the exercise bank provides unusually deep identification, construction and ear-training practice.
marginal_value: Adds formal theory and deliberate drill practice that the Ableton creation courses do not replace.

learning_need: Transferable digital-product and visual-design foundations with practical exercises
decision_rationale: Figma clearly wins the general digital-design comparison. The course goes beyond tool onboarding into audience research, ethics, accessibility, UI design, prototyping, design systems, wireframing, grids, color and composition with practical exercises.
marginal_value: Adds a substantive transferable digital-design foundation rather than a short vendor tutorial.
provider_concentration_notes: Figma is not otherwise concentrated in the canonical set.
coverage_notes: Becomes the primary digital-design route; Canva remains a useful microcourse but not a core slot.

learning_need: Animation, storytelling and technical-art reasoning through authentic production problems
decision_rationale: Pixar in a Box remains exceptional because it teaches transferable creative/technical reasoning rather than a single software package. Fifteen units and 69 skills connect storytelling, lighting, simulation, color science, cameras, rigging, animation, modelling and rendering to authentic Pixar problems.
marginal_value: Adds deep animation/storytelling and production reasoning that complements a current real-time toolchain.
provider_concentration_notes: Khan also appears in Art History, but these are clearly separate learning roles.
coverage_notes: Complements Unity rather than competing directly: Pixar teaches transferable production concepts; Unity teaches implementation in a current engine.

learning_need: Zero-experience onboarding to real-time 3D creation in Unity
decision_rationale: Unity Essentials earns a slot as the explicit beginner entry to the creative Unity pathway. Its two-week project-led structure introduces GameObjects, scenes, prefabs, materials and editor workflows, and it materially lowers the prerequisite barrier to Creative Core.
marginal_value: Adds a true zero-beginner real-time 3D onboarding route that the more advanced Creative Core and coding-focused Junior Programmer do not replace.
provider_concentration_notes: Unity concentration is controlled by role: beginner creative onboarding, deeper creative production and programming are distinct pathways.
coverage_notes: Forms a coherent sequence into Creative Core; complements the canonical Junior Programmer coding pathway.

learning_need: Project-heavy real-time 3D creative production across materials, lighting, animation, VFX, audio and UI
decision_rationale: Creative Core is the strongest current real-time 3D creative pathway in the pool. Its ten-week Unity 6.x curriculum combines guided and independent projects across materials, lighting, animation, VFX, cameras, post-processing, audio, UI and prototyping.
marginal_value: Adds a deep portfolio-oriented creative-production path distinct from programming and from Pixar's transferable production concepts.
provider_concentration_notes: The second Arts Unity slot is justified as the substantive continuation after Essentials; Junior Programmer remains a separate coding role.
coverage_notes: Pairs with Essentials as a sequence and with Pixar in a Box as conceptual/creative complement.

learning_need: Broad global art history and visual analysis
decision_rationale: Khan AP/College Art History is the broad category leader for art history. It spans ancient Mediterranean, Europe, Africa, Asia, Indigenous Americas, the Pacific and global contemporary traditions with strong visual-analysis materials and embedded practice.
marginal_value: Adds a global art-history backbone with much broader geographic and chronological coverage than the narrow visual-source alternative.
provider_concentration_notes: Second Khan Arts slot is justified by a separate academic art-history role from Pixar's production curriculum.

learning_need: Career and business practice for creative freelancers
decision_rationale: A freelance career in the creative arts adds a professional-practice role absent from the technical and art-history courses. Its 24-hour sequence covers strengths, networks, audiences, promotion, investment, business structures and business-plan development with weekly quizzes and planning work.
marginal_value: Adds career sustainability and business planning specifically for creative practitioners.
provider_concentration_notes: OpenLearn appears widely across the index, but this is a distinct creative-career role rather than another content course.
coverage_notes: Tax/legal/platform details need monitoring because the course was last updated in 2021; the broader career-planning pedagogy remains useful.

learning_need: Very short certified introduction to graphic-design principles
decision_rationale: Canva Graphic Design Essentials is current and legitimate, but 53 minutes is too little depth for a separate core slot when Figma provides a much broader transferable design curriculum with stronger practice. The free certificate does not compensate for scope.
marginal_value: Adds low-friction onboarding and a certificate but insufficient sustained learning.
provider_concentration_notes: Provider concentration is not the deciding factor.
coverage_notes: Graphic-design foundations remain covered more substantively by the Figma route.

learning_need: Visual-source criticism through historical family photography
decision_rationale: Picturing the family is thoughtful and useful, but its narrow photographic-source role is already substantially covered by the broader Khan art-history visual-analysis route and the canonical OpenLearn historical-method course. Its older currentness score further reduces marginal value.
marginal_value: Adds focused family-photography interpretation but not enough unique core coverage.
provider_concentration_notes: OpenLearn concentration reinforces the redundancy decision.
coverage_notes: Remains a reviewed specialist for learners specifically interested in family photography as historical evidence.
